1  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 18.12.2003 passed by the Motor Accident Claims NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2559/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined Tribunal, (Main) Navsari in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.295 of 2021 by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with 10% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable jointly and severally.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 The claimants filed the claim petition stating that on 4.2.1997, the deceased was driving his Suzuki Motorcycle towards his home Nimlai and when he reached near S.M.Factory being situated on Ubhraat road, one S.T.Bus bearing registration no.GJ.1Z.3521 which was on its way from Maroli to Navsari, came from the opposite direction, being driven by his driver in an excessive speed and in a rash and negligent manner and it came on its extreme wrong side of the road and dashed with the motorcycle of the deceased, as a result of which the deceased received grievous injuries and he wa taken to the hospital and he succumbed during the treatment.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the claimants for compensation.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
The opponents appeared and filed their written statements denying the contents of the claim petition.

The Tribunal has framed the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2559/2007 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above. 2.3
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the present appeal is preferred by the appellant-GSRTC.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant-insurance company has assailed the impugned judgment and award on the ground of negligence and quantum, more particularly,
that looking to the manner in which the accident occurred, the driver of the motorcycle should have been held solely negligent for the accident or atleast contributory negligence should have been apportioned between both the vehicles;
that the ratio of negligence is attributed with the notion that the heavy vehicle can be offender vehicle and accepted the case of the respondents-claimants and that the accident occurred solely due to the breach of traffic rules on the part of the deceased.
4.
Further, on the point of quantum also, the learned Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation on higher NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2559/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined side.
He, therefore, submitted to allow this appeal on both these counts.

G.S.R.T.C vs Sarlaben Balwantbhai Patel on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26799906/
2 5.
Per contra, learned advocate for the claimants has submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper and is not required to be interfered with.

He submitted that the deceased was driving his motorcycle on the correct side the road,
however, the ST bus came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner in excessive speed and dashed with the motorcycle of the deceased and therefore, the learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence led before it, came to the conclusion that the ST bus was solely negligent for the accident, which is just and proper and not required to be interfered with.

He submitted that even on the point of quantum, the learned Tribunal has considered the evidence and awarded the amount of compensation, which is just and proper and therefore this appeal be dismissed.
6. I have considered the submissions made at the bar and also gone through the material produced on record, including the impugned judgment and award.

7. As regards the first contention of holding the ST bus driver solely negligent for the accident, from the FIR and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2559/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined panchanama, indicate the manner in which the accident has occurred and it indicates that the ST bus was lying on the right side facing towards Maroli and the motorcycle was lying beneath the front wheel of the bus which indicate that the motorcycle ran over the said motorcycle and the driver of the bus applied the brakes and brake marks were visible at about 30 feet behind the bus.
Further, there were two eye witnesses to the incident who were examined by the claimants who have also supported the say of the claimants.

One of the eye witness viz. Naginbhai Naranbhai deposed that the deceased was proceeding from Maroli to Ubhraat and at that time, one ST bus was coming from Ubhraat i.e. from the opposite direction and driver of the ST bus dashed with the deceased by driving the bus on wrong side and committed the accident.

Another witness who lodged the complaint stated that he noticed that on Maroli-Ubhraat road, the accident occurred and the driver of ST bus has driven his bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed with the motorcycle and committed the accident.

Therefore, after discussing the said evidence in detail, the learned Tribunal has held the ST bus driver 100%
negligent for the accident, which is not required to be interfered with by this Court in this appeal.
This appeal is, therefore, required to be dismissed on this ground.

8. On the point of quantum, from the discussion made on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2559/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the point of quantum in the impugned judgment, in paragraphs 14 to 19, the learned Tribunal has discussed that the income is taken on the basis of salary certificate produced and considering the age of the deceased, arrived at just and proper compensation by considering the evidence led before it and the ratio laid down in various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which is just and proper and is not required to be interfered with in this appeal.
9. In view of the above, this appeal is required to be dismissed and therefore, the following order is passed.

10. In view of above, the following order is passed.
10.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.

10.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
10.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J)
